meta.title: Slots and overrides
meta.description: Every replaceable part of the component, what a slot receives, and a worked example.

intro: A slot replaces the component of a part while keeping its place, its props and its behavior. Your component receives everything the built-in one would have had:
rules: Spread the props you are given. They carry the class names, the data attribute, the event handlers and the accessible name.
Attach the ref when there is one: pinning, measuring and focus depend on it.
ownerState says what the part is rendering for — the view, the scheme, the item, the shift — so one slot can behave differently in the list and in the timeline.
Default is the built-in component, if you want to wrap it rather than replace it.
A render prop wins over a slot for the same content: renderItem replaces the whole card, and then the card’s own parts are yours to draw.
